definitions.explanation: A container or dish used for holding food, drink, or other items. Often refers to pottery, ceramics, or tableware with aesthetic value.
A person's capacity, caliber, or suitability for a role. Used figuratively to describe whether someone has the personal qualities needed for a position or responsibility.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}を{美|うつく}しい{器|うつわ}に{盛|も}り{付|つ}けた。
examples.english: I arranged the food on a beautiful dish.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{器|うつわ}にもこだわっている。
examples.english: This restaurant is particular about its tableware too.

examples.japanese: {陶芸|とうげい}{教室|きょうしつ}で{自分|じぶん}だけの{器|うつわ}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made my own pottery dish at a ceramics class.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はリーダーの{器|うつわ}だ。
examples.english: He has the caliber to be a leader.

examples.japanese: {器|うつわ}の{大|おお}きい{人|ひと}になりたい。
examples.english: I want to become a person of great character.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}の{器|うつわ}ではないと{自分|じぶん}でも{分|わ}かっている。
examples.english: I know myself that I'm not cut out to be president.

notes:
In sense 1, {器|うつわ} is closely associated with Japanese food culture and aesthetics — the presentation of food on carefully chosen {器|うつわ} is considered an important part of the dining experience.

In sense 2, {器|うつわ}が{大|おお}きい (big vessel) means someone is generous and broad-minded, while {器|うつわ}が{小|ちい}さい (small vessel) means someone is petty or narrow-minded.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{器|うつわ}に{盛|も}る — to serve in a dish
・{器|うつわ}が{大|おお}きい — broad-minded, magnanimous
・{器|うつわ}が{小|ちい}さい — petty, narrow-minded
・リーダーの{器|うつわ} — the caliber of a leader
・{焼|や}き{物|もの}の{器|うつわ} — pottery dishes
